sentences.text: To bring home the guilt of the accused persons the prosecution has examined CW.1 by name Kiran Kumar as PW.1.

The PW.1 has deposed that in the year 2005 he had filed a suit in O.S.
No.471/2005 before the Prl. Senior Civil Judge, Bengaluru.
In the year 2006 the said suit was transferred to Devanahalli Court as O.S. No.2222/2006.
For the said case, he had engaged accused No.1 and 2 as his advocates.
They told him to pay the court fee of Rs.17,125/- and including their fees he paid Rs.40,000/- to them on 18.02.2005.
On 19.02.2005, they filed case before the court.
On 05.03.2005 C.C. No.9033/2015 matter came before the Hon'ble Court and passed status quo order against the defendants.
He has furher deposed that on 07.03.2005 accused No.2 withdrawn the DD which is supposed to be paid to the court.
He had taken the said DD in the name of court only.

He came to know about the above said fact in the year 2013 when the proposed defendants filed objection stating that in the plaint they have mentioned Rs.17,125/- as court fee but actually they have paid Rs.75/-.
The same is found in the valuation slip as they had corrected it.
They also altered the same in plaint.
As the accused No.1 and 2 were not appearing regularly before the Devanahalli Court therefore by filing the memo he had changed the Advocate and appointed Advocate D.A Lakshmi as his counsel.
After verifying the materials, Devanahalli Court told them that the court fee paid by them is insufficient therefore they have to pay the balance court fee.
Accordingly he paid the balance court fee amount and continued the matter.
Later with the help of his Advocate he came to City Civil Court and verified his original DD encashment.
The bank official told that the said DD got encashed by accused No.2, he gave complaint to Halsur Gate Police Station.

The admission given by PW.1 in his cross- examination shows that there are no documents to prove that complainant had given Rs.40,000/- to the accused No.1 and 2.

In the complaint lodged by the complainant dated 10.01.2014 he has mentioned that on 18.02.2005 he had paid Rs.40,000/-
to the advocate fees for filing the suit and court fees of Rs.17,125/-.

He has further mentioned in complaint that in the year 2013 the defendants have filed application for dismissal of suit as only Rs.75/- was paid as court fees, whereas Rs.17,125/- was to be paid as court fees.

He has also mentioned that the accused persons have struck off Rs.17,125/- and written Rs.75/- without the orders of the court and removed Demand Draft from the court custody instead of crediting the proceeds to court account and handed over to the advocate Veena. B who got canceled the DD and fraudulently encashed the proceeds.
. The evidence of PW.1 is quite contrary to the contents of complaint.
In the complaint it is mentioned that on 19.02.2005 DD was brought for Rs.17,125/- by Veena. B, but in the evidence the PW.1 has stated that DD was brought by him in his name.
The prosecution has itself produced Ex.P.4 which clearly shows that in O.S. No.471/2005 a valuation slip showing Rs.75/- as court fees was paid dated 05.03.2005.

The Ex.P.6 is also the valuation slip filed in O.S.No.471/2005, wherein some correction are made in all the columns of valuation slip, wherein some writings are stricken out and some entries are made.
On perusal of Ex.P.6 it shows that under Section 7(2) of the Karnataka Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act court fees of Rs.75/- was paid.

No doubt there are some over writings in Ex.P.6, but the Ex.P.4 clearly shows that as per Section 7(2) (A) of the Karnataka Court Fees and Suit Valuation Act court fees of Rs.75/- was paid.

sentences.text: The Ex.P.4 is not denied by the complainant.

As stated above the admission given by the PW.1 M.Kirankumar vs D.K.Nagaraju on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45289387/

Though the learned APP for the prosecution cross- C.C. No.9033/2015 examination DW-1 and DW-2 at length nothing is elicited to show that the Accused No. 1 and 2 have cheated the CW-1 or to prove that the CW- 1 had given RS 40,000/- to the Accused No. 1 and 2 towards court fees and advocates fee.
Perusal of the contents of the complaint shows that this complaint is an afterthought of the complainant.
There are no evidence on record to hold that the Accused No. 1 and 2 in collusion with the court staff have lifted the DD from the court.

The documents shows that the DD was never presented before the court and that there is no mention of either DD number or DD amount in any of the documents submitted by the prosecution relating to the suit in which the Accused No. 1 and 2 had filed vakalat for the present complainant.

When the DD was never present before the court and as the DD was never issued in the name of the complainant the question of the Accused No. 1 and 2 fraudulently cheating the CW- 1 with intention to cheat him does not arise.
The records show that the DD was issued in the name of Accused No. 2 and it was got cancelled by her.
No evidence is placed by prosecution to prove that the D amount as given by the CW- 1 to the Accused No. 2.
the documents produced by the Accused No. 1 and 2 are not C.C. No.9033/2015 rebutted by the prosecution.
Absolutely there are no materials on record to attract the penal provision under Section 420 IPC.
Even the investigating officer has not made efforts to get the expert opinion in respect of Exh.P-1.
The mahazar witness are not examined.
21. On appreciating the entire evidence of all the prosecution witness the evidence transpires that none of the ingredients required for convicting a person under alleged section are attracted.
The evidence of PW-1 is self serving statement and inconsistent with his own case.
Having considered the oral evidence I am constrained to conclude that the prosecution has not established that the accused have cheated the PW- 1.
Thus the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Therefore, this court answers point No.1 in the Negative.

22. Point No. 2:- For the aforesaid reasons, this court proceed to pass the following:

The documents shows that the DD was never presented before the court and that there is no mention of either DD number or DD amount in any of the documents submitted by the prosecution relating to the suit in which the Accused No. 1 and 2 had filed vakalat for the present complainant.
When the DD was never present before the court and as the DD was never issued in the name of the complainant the question of the Accused No. 1 and 2 fraudulently cheating the CW- 1 with intention to cheat him does not arise.
The records show that the DD was issued in the name of Accused No. 2 and it was got cancelled by her.
No evidence is placed by prosecution to prove that the D amount as given by the CW- 1 to the Accused No. 2.
the documents produced by the Accused No. 1 and 2 are not C.C. No.9033/2015 rebutted by the prosecution.
Absolutely there are no materials on record to attract the penal provision under Section 420 IPC.
21. On appreciating the entire evidence of all the prosecution witness the evidence transpires that none of the ingredients required for convicting a person under alleged section are attracted.
The evidence of PW-1 is self serving statement and inconsistent with his own case.
Having considered the oral evidence I am constrained to conclude that the prosecution has not established that the accused have cheated the PW- 1.
Thus the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
